purpose: Cross-corpus taxonomy observations and research questions; not a canonical glossary or source VNext
coverage: Initial seed only. Corpus-wide and FG-TIDA audit is not complete.
authorship: AI-assisted analysis; no independent review or external adoption implied.
authority: Changes to source meanings remain in each owning VNext and require the applicable owner decision.

observations.title: Taxonomy, terminology, glossary and ontology are different work products
observations.observation: A list of terms, a classification and a relational model answer different questions. Whether the initiative needs each is a design question, not a new universal definition.
observations.next_question_or_test: Compare a term list, a classification with overlapping members and a relation-bearing model; record what each cannot answer.

observations.title: Programme, architectural contribution and technical gates are different levels
observations.observation: Calling Structural Awareness, Ecosystem Positioning, EA, RA and MSCA interchangeable hides which source and function supports a claim.
observations.next_question_or_test: Trace one claim from programme narrative to its owning architecture/gate and name the actual supporting source.

observations.title: A/B/C/D should not become four mutually exclusive bins
observations.observation: A represented item not yet consulted must not automatically become C. The qualification depends on process, subject, decision and time; it is not an exhaustive population partition.
observations.next_question_or_test: Test a known, evaluable but unconsulted record; record the subject/process/time rather than reclassifying it as an intrinsically unknown object.

observations.title: Type 0 is not another management-failure class
observations.observation: Structural non-determination, management failures and ensuing trajectories must not be added as if they were classes of the same kind.
observations.next_question_or_test: Classify a non-determination, a Type1/2 event and a cascade without treating them as three peer failure labels.

observations.title: Representation state is not assessment state
observations.observation: An unpopulated representation and an unassessed sufficiency claim are different absences. Schema completeness does not establish support.
observations.next_question_or_test: Use a fully populated but unevaluated instance and an empty instance; neither should silently become SUPPORTED.

observations.title: S/E/C/P/M are semantic slots, not five software modules
observations.observation: Treating the kernel slots as deployable components or silently adding a sixth canonical element would change the architecture rather than clarify a label.
observations.next_question_or_test: Ask for one implementation mapping of each slot, with an explicit statement that the mapping is not the canonical definition.

observations.title: Role, position, capability, mandate and permission are not synonyms
observations.observation: A capability-bearing participant is not thereby authorized. A functional projection and a qualified epistemic position answer different questions.
observations.next_question_or_test: Use a capable but unauthorized participant, and an authorized but unavailable participant.

observations.title: RA collides: Regime Awareness versus Remote Attestation
observations.observation: The same short token refers to two different concepts in the combined corpus. Text matching alone cannot justify a mapping.
observations.next_question_or_test: Require an expanded name and source namespace on first use; reject Regime Awareness = Remote Attestation.

observations.title: Observed delta, receiver gradient and operational posture are different objects
observations.observation: A qualified directional change is not an executed containment action or a receiver-specific migration destination.
observations.next_question_or_test: Trace producer output to receiver decision and observed action; identify which transition is not licensed by a change signal.

observations.title: P1/P2/P3 postures collide with P1–P6 principle identifiers
observations.observation: A short P identifier can denote an operational posture or a principle, depending on its source family. This is a candidate occurrence audit, not an approved renaming.
observations.next_question_or_test: Inventory occurrences and preserve existing source identifiers; qualify new references by family.

observations.title: DDS stages and local gates/testbed stages need namespaces
observations.observation: DDS A/B/C, local Stage-0/Stage-1 and R-number families are source-specific. A shared number is not a universal translation rule.
observations.next_question_or_test: Build a source-specific stage mapping including a deliberately mismatched Stage1 pair that must remain unmapped.

observations.title: RL Trajectory/Verifier do not erase other domain meanings
observations.observation: The reinforcement-learning meanings proposed in Theme52 do not supersede DDS trajectories or credential/evidence verification.
observations.next_question_or_test: Compare one RL trajectory/verifier example with a DDS and a credential-verifier example; preserve non-equivalence.

observations.title: Policy has multiple authored objects and scopes
observations.observation: Deployment configuration, an authored evaluation reference and jurisdictional requirements may all be called policy; their authors and change authorities can differ.
observations.next_question_or_test: Record originator, jurisdiction/domain, applicable version and authority to change each policy object.

observations.title: A flag taxonomy is not a cross-evaluator failure taxonomy
observations.observation: A collection of flags measured by one evaluator and a classification of failures between evaluators have different universes and observation units.
observations.next_question_or_test: State the classified universe and observation unit before combining any categories.

observations.title: Trust, trustworthiness, evidence and reliance remain distinct questions
observations.observation: Contributed definitions in Theme51 and meeting discussions do not establish a single accepted meaning or make reliance a measured property.
observations.next_question_or_test: Record rival definitions and one decision that differs between them; do not settle the dispute by frequency of the word.

observations.title: Identity must not collapse principal, instance and legal binding
observations.observation: Authentication, logical identity, represented principal, runtime instance and legal binding require different evidence. A signature cannot fill all missing links.
observations.next_question_or_test: Use a valid signature with unknown principal authorization and legal scope; retain those gaps.

observations.title: Available, presented, noticed and understood evidence are different claims
observations.observation: Evidence can exist without being shown, and be shown without evidence of comprehension. Do not turn this into an automatic ladder of approval.
observations.next_question_or_test: Use a delivered document with no evidence of comprehension; keep shown and understood independent.

observations.title: Finding, sufficiency judgment and authorized decision are different steps
observations.observation: A finding may support a scoped judgment without giving the recipient permission to act. Support, inference and authorization are different relations.
observations.next_question_or_test: Use a scoped experimental PASS with no applicable action authority.

observations.title: Applicable authority does not establish timely capacity
observations.observation: A named decision maker may lack information, access, availability or time. External queue overload is not by itself local incompetence.
observations.next_question_or_test: Keep authority, capability, information access and useful intervention time separate in a specific escalation example.

observations.title: Acknowledgment, attempted action and observed effect are not equivalent
observations.observation: Receipt or acknowledgement does not establish that the intended effect occurred. Repeating or signing a claim does not make its observation independent.
observations.next_question_or_test: Use an ACK with no independent effect evidence; preserve the missing observation and time window.

observations.title: Epistemic validity and response opportunity use different clocks
observations.observation: A still-valid finding can arrive too late for a useful action; spare time cannot make stale findings current. Synthetic timestamps do not establish measured latency.
observations.next_question_or_test: Use a valid-but-late result and a stale-but-fast result; neither implies the other clock passed.

observations.title: Historical authenticity is not present applicability
observations.observation: Preserve the original finding while requalifying the present use affected by a changed dependency or context.
observations.next_question_or_test: Link a historical authentic result to a present use that is no longer supported, without changing the old result.

observations.title: Changed conditions and changed relevance boundaries are different problems
observations.observation: A monitored variable can change, or a previously unrepresented factor can become material without changing the old source bytes. Monitoring does not prove complete coverage.
observations.next_question_or_test: Contrast ordinary drift with a relevance-boundary change; specify the discovery limit and unknown residual.

observations.title: Human Intelligence Debt is not runtime intervention capacity
observations.observation: The architectural use of human intelligence and whether a specific intervention route can act now need separate units, estimators and claims.
observations.next_question_or_test: Use a runtime queue delay without inferring a universal intelligence-debt score.

observations.title: Principle, requirement, hypothesis, condition and KPI need claim types
observations.observation: Document placement does not turn a hypothesis into proof or make a KPI a requirement. S/T/H families need source-qualified interpretation.
observations.next_question_or_test: Trace a hypothesis through its requirement and measurement consumers; retain its actual proof/execution status.

observations.title: Current, candidate, test-only and adopted need separate status axes
observations.observation: Source description, candidate interface field, test evidence and institutional adoption are not successive states established merely by publication.
observations.next_question_or_test: Try mapping a test-only field to adopted and require rejection unless the actual decision evidence exists.

observations.title: Thematic coverage is not evidential coverage
observations.observation: A theme/coverage map can locate a question without demonstrating its specification, implementation or resolution.
observations.next_question_or_test: Keep conceptual, specification, implementation and evidence coverage as four views with explicit gaps.

observations.title: Cross-WG terminology is an opportunity, not an appointment or accepted slot
observations.observation: The meeting record describes potential terminology support. It does not appoint a lead, grant a contribution slot or authorize an external submission.
observations.next_question_or_test: Recheck current procedural conditions before any external approach; record no appointment or submission from this entry.

observations.title: Same-label semantic change needs versioned consumer review
observations.observation: A label can remain stable while scope, criterion or decision consequences change. A global word replacement would hide consumer compatibility questions.
observations.next_question_or_test: Select one real meaning change and its consumers; propose a versioned mapping before any source correction.

observations.title: Flattened unknown-like statuses can lose decision-relevant reasons
observations.observation: INDETERMINATE, no-assertion, HELD, UNKNOWN, not-evaluated and not-applicable can encode different reasons. A single unknown may change an action boundary.
observations.next_question_or_test: Construct a mapping with a positive preservation example and a reason-losing negative example before declaring equivalence.

ideas.title: Federated concept architecture
ideas.proposal: Keep a small shared core, source-owned domain vocabularies and explicit crosswalks; do not force a universal hierarchy.

ideas.title: Separate classification axes
ideas.proposal: Represent object kind, epistemic state, authority, time, evidence and document maturity independently.

ideas.title: Meaning-preserving crosswalks
ideas.proposal: Represent exact, narrower, broader, related, incompatible and unresolved relationships explicitly; no untested automatic equivalence.

ideas.title: Decision-oriented minimal pairs
ideas.proposal: Prioritize examples where two readings produce different permissions, sufficiency judgments or consumer decisions.

ideas.title: Source-qualified identifiers
ideas.proposal: Use stable concept/sense IDs and source namespaces while retaining historical labels and acronyms.

ideas.title: Version-aware consumer impact
ideas.proposal: Review descendants of a changed meaning without invalidating independent support paths or rewriting historical findings.

ideas.title: Bilingual and metaphor review
ideas.proposal: Track translation and explanatory wording separately from technical definitions; show what is lost.

ideas.title: Coverage by collection and surface
ideas.proposal: Include the full own programme and FG-TIDA files, issues, comments, PRs and linked annexes; keep exclusions visible.

ideas.title: Review tests without semantic overclaim
ideas.proposal: Use positive and negative mapping examples; machine-readable consistency is not conceptual truth or external validation.

ideas.title: Incremental public PR practice
ideas.proposal: Small linked PRs with evidence, objections and owner decisions; preserve disagreements and reuse each source's existing VNext.
